components.css: .ds-sheet{background:var(--panel,#1f2328);border:3px solid var(--rule-strong,#eef0f2);color:var(--ink,#eef0f2);font:500 15px/1.5 var(--font,Outfit,sans-serif);max-width:560px}.ds-sheet-head{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;gap:12px;padding:12px 18px;border-bottom:1.5px solid var(--rule,rgba(238,240,242,.22))}.ds-title{margin:0;font:700 22px/.95 var(--font,Outfit,sans-serif);text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:-.02em}.ds-label{font:400 12px var(--mono,'DM Mono',monospace);letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-2,rgba(238,240,242,.74))}.ds-status{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:8px}.ds-lamp{display:inline-block;width:10px;height:10px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--ok,#4fe06a)}.ds-lamp.is-partial{background:var(--partial,#f5c12e)}.ds-lamp.is-failed{background:var(--failed,#ff5a4a)}.ds-lamp.is-off{background:var(--off,#4a5059)}.ds-parts{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0}.ds-parts li{border-bottom:1px dotted var(--rule,rgba(238,240,242,.22))}.ds-parts li:last-child{border-bottom:0}.ds-part{display:grid;grid-template-columns:30px minmax(0,1fr) auto 12px;align-items:center;gap:14px;padding:11px 18px;transition:background-color .2s cubic-bezier(.37,0,.63,1);cursor:pointer}.ds-part:hover{background:var(--raised,#272c33)}.ds-name{font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.02em;line-height:1.25}.ds-name small{display:block;font-weight:500;text-transform:none;letter-spacing:0;font-size:13px;color:var(--ink-2,rgba(238,240,242,.74))}.ds-spec{text-align:right}.ds-spec.is-custom{color:var(--accent-text,#ff7a33)}.ds-balloon{width:28px;height:28px;border-radius:50%;border:2px solid var(--balloon,#62a3ea);display:grid;place-items:center;font:500 12px var(--mono,'DM Mono',monospace)}.ds-balloon.is-sequential{border-color:var(--serial,#f5c12e)}.ds-balloon.is-unordered{border-style:dashed}

narrative.overview:
Every managed playlist is an assembly drawing and every show in it is a numbered part. The part's spec is its resolved rule ("Latest only · newest", "Up to 2 · oldest · sequential"), set in the same mono a drawing uses for callouts, so the screen states exactly what the next rebuild will do. The interface is a bill of materials, not a dashboard: square-cornered sheets with a heavy edge, ballooned numbers, status lamps that always carry their word, and one orange signal.

It is calm, cool and dense. Grounds are graphite (dark) or drawing-sheet grey (light), never warm. Outfit in heavy uppercase names things; DM Mono in tracked uppercase labels and specifies them. Ant Design stays underneath and is restyled entirely through theme tokens and a thin layer of overrides, so every Ant control speaks the same language as the custom part rows. The app belongs to the Marcus Lab family through its mark, its two typefaces and its voice, not through the family's brown palette, and it never looks like an official Spotify product.

The opening view, the Run sheet, answers "did last night work?" from a strip of facts before anything is clicked, then lays out every playlist as an assembly so a wrong rule or an unreachable show is visible in its own row.
keyCharacteristics: Square sheets with a 3px full-ink edge; 1.5px rules between sections; 1px dotted dividers between rows.
Numbered balloons (blue ring; amber ring for sequential shows; dashed ring when order is not used).
Status as lamp plus word, never colour alone.
One orange signal: primary action, current nav, custom and sequential specs, focus.
Pills for everything you press; squares for everything you read.
Light and dark themes are equals and both ship.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange marks only what you press next, where you are, and a spec that differs from the default. If two orange fills are on screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Lamp-and-Word Rule
rules.body: A status lamp never appears without its word (OK, Partial, Failed, Off, Not run yet) or an accessible label; colour is the second channel, not the only one.

rules.name: The Cool Ground Rule
rules.body: Grounds are cool graphite or cool grey. The Marcus Lab warm brown grounds are ruled out, and so is Spotify green.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Outfit names, DM Mono specifies. A rule, a state word or a measurement is set in mono; a thing the user owns (a show, a playlist) is set in Outfit uppercase.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Numbers that line up (tables, statistics, run sheet figures) use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Drawn Edge Rule
rules.body: If something needs to stand apart, give it an edge or a tone step, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Press-Round, Read-Square Rule
rules.body: Round corners belong only to pills, balloons and lamps. A panel with a radius is out of system.

dos: Do restyle Ant Design through `themeConfig.ts` tokens and the `.pm-*` vocabulary in `index.css`, keeping the CSS custom properties and the theme palette in step.
Do draw every playlist as a sheet of numbered parts with the resolved rule as each part's spec (The Two Voices Rule).
Do show status as lamp plus word, with the reason in a tooltip or problem line (The Lamp-and-Word Rule).
Do keep orange to the primary action, the current nav item, custom or sequential specs and focus (The One Signal Rule).
Do use a 3px full-ink edge for objects, 1.5px rules for structure and 1px dotted lines between rows.
Do design and check light and dark together; they are equals. iOS takes only these colours and Outfit/DM Mono, through native SwiftUI components.
Do keep every motion behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
donts: Don't round panels, cards, tables or inputs; round is for pills, balloons and lamps only (The Press-Round, Read-Square Rule).
Don't add resting or hover shadows, gradients or glows (The Drawn Edge Rule).
Don't reintroduce the Marcus Lab brown grounds or Spotify green, and never use the Spotify logo, Circular or a Spotify-style layout.
Don't add a second accent: Balloon Blue rings balloons and nothing else.
Don't put a mono kicker or eyebrow above a page title; the date or context line goes beneath it.
Don't bring the project page's navy, marigold or Familjen Grotesk into the app.
